themes_detail.label: Indoor Air Quality Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Indoor air quality complaints spiked to 6 this week versus a baseline of 0.9 per week—a 586% increase (z-score: 4.87)—suggesting a potential environmental hazard affecting multiple buildings in Hunts Point/Longwood this week.
evidence: 6 indoor air quality complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.9 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (586% spike, z-score 4.87)
Concurrent outdoor air quality spike last week: 4 complaints vs. 0.6 weekly average (540% increase, z-score 4.85)
Timing suggests possible shared environmental trigger (industrial emission, building ventilation failure, or external pollution event)
reporting_angles: Investigate whether complaints cluster around specific buildings or industrial facilities; identify what triggered simultaneous indoor/outdoor air quality failures
Interview affected residents about symptoms and timeline; cross-reference with DEP air quality monitoring data and industrial activities in the district

themes_detail.label: Rodent Infestation Surge
themes_detail.summary: Rodent complaints more than tripled to 6 last week from a baseline of 1.5 per week—a 300% jump (z-score: 4.5)—indicating a potential infestation problem spreading across the district last week.
evidence: 6 rodent complaints last week vs. 1.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (300% spike, z-score 4.5)
Aligns with ongoing 'UNSANITARY CONDITION' complaints (496 total over 90 days), suggesting sanitation issues may be enabling pest spread
Community Board has repeatedly requested expanded building inspector capacity—a signal this district has chronic infrastructure/maintenance gaps
reporting_angles: Map rodent complaint locations to identify whether infestation is building-specific or neighborhood-wide; interview HPD about recent violations
Examine connection between building maintenance failures and rodent problems; investigate whether understaffed DOB inspector corps is preventing timely enforcement

themes_detail.label: Curb and Street Condition Collapse
themes_detail.summary: Curb condition complaints jumped to 3 this week from a baseline of 0.1 per week—a 2300% spike (z-score: 8.69)—indicating rapid deterioration of street infrastructure in Hunts Point/Longwood this week.
evidence: 3 curb condition complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (2300% spike, z-score 8.69)
Concurrent spike in street sign damage/missing signs 3 weeks ago (up 967–2300%), suggesting broader street infrastructure stress
Community Board has no recent ULURP or capital project data addressing street maintenance—gap may indicate deferred repairs
reporting_angles: Document which blocks show worst curb damage via photo survey; request DOT inspection data and repair backlog for the district
Investigate whether recent potholes or utility work disrupted street integrity; connect to pedestrian safety and ADA accessibility concerns

themes_detail.label: Elevator System Failures
themes_detail.summary: Elevator complaints jumped to 22 three weeks ago from a baseline of 7.8 per week—a 184% increase (z-score: 4.12)—signaling widespread mechanical failures in residential buildings three weeks ago.
evidence: 22 elevator complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 7.8 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (184% spike, z-score 4.12)
Hunts Point/Longwood has aging multifamily stock; elevator failures disproportionately affect elderly and disabled residents in high-rises
Community Board budget requests include 'assign additional building inspectors'—suggests chronic DOB capacity gap affecting preventive maintenance oversight
reporting_angles: Identify buildings with repeated elevator failures; interview DOB about inspection frequency and enforcement against landlords
Profile impact on seniors and disabled residents trapped in buildings with broken elevators; connect to broader housing maintenance crisis

themes_detail.label: Heat and Hot Water Crisis (Baseline Concern)
themes_detail.summary: Heat/hot water remains the district's dominant 311 complaint category with 2,380 complaints over 90 days, indicating a chronic winterization and building maintenance crisis affecting hundreds of households throughout the survey period.
evidence: 2,380 heat/hot water complaints over 90 days—by far the largest complaint category, representing >40% of all complaints tracked
Indicates sustained failure of building heating systems affecting the entire district through fall/winter season
Community Board lacks recent capital budget allocation for building system upgrades—suggests deferred maintenance at scale
reporting_angles: Conduct survey of residents without heat; identify buildings with repeat violations and absent landlords
Investigate HPD enforcement record: how many fines issued, collected, and used for emergency repairs versus remediation?
